system.system_purpose: Small service that receives deployment events from an external continuous-integration platform and posts them to an internal chat channel so engineers see deploys without watching the CI dashboard.

claims.value: Receives deployment events from an external CI platform and posts them to an internal chat channel so engineers can see deploys without watching the CI dashboard.
Deployment events come from an external continuous-integration platform and are delivered to the Deploy Notifier.
Deployment events are posted to an internal chat channel via the chat platform's API.

claims.rationale: The documentation explicitly states that no customer data passes through the notifier.
The event handling and data sections state that deployment events name repositories, environments, and commit identifiers, and that the receiver reads these fields.

claims.value: Public HTTPS endpoint that receives deployment events as JSON from the CI platform, parses them, and hands them to the notifier.

claims.rationale: The component is described as a public HTTPS endpoint that the CI platform calls.

claims.value: Formats deployment events and posts them to the internal chat channel over the chat platform's API.

claims.rationale: The CI platform delivers each deployment event as a JSON body to the receiver's public URL.
The receiver accepts and processes any well-formed delivery and does not check a signature.

Although the CI platform supports signing deliveries with a shared secret, the receiver does not check a signature and accepts any well-formed delivery, so there is no documented mechanism for authenticating the event source at the application level.
The Event Receiver is described as a public HTTPS endpoint, implying HTTP over TLS for inbound webhook deliveries.

claims.value: External continuous-integration service that sends deployment events to the notifier.
Internal reader of the chat channel where deployment notifications are posted.

claims.rationale: The documentation states that the Chat Notifier posts to the chat platform's API but does not describe how those API calls are authenticated.
The documentation does not describe any authorization model or access-control rules for the Deploy Notifier.
Deployment events are described as naming repositories, environments, and commit identifiers and explicitly not including customer data, so they are treated as internal operational data.

components.name: Event Receiver
components.description: Public HTTPS endpoint that the external CI platform calls with deployment events as JSON; it parses the events and hands them to the notifier.

components.name: Chat Notifier
components.description: Formats deployment events and posts messages naming the repository, environment, and commit to the internal chat channel via the chat platform's API.

components.name: CI Platform
components.description: External continuous-integration service that sends deployment events as JSON webhooks to the Event Receiver and supports signing deliveries with a shared secret.

components.name: Chat Platform
components.description: Chat platform whose API is used to post deployment notifications to an internal chat channel.

assets.name: Deployment event data
assets.description: Deployment events containing repository names, environments, and commit identifiers sent from the CI platform and delivered through the notifier to the chat channel.

data_flows.name: CI platform to Event Receiver webhook
Event Receiver to Chat Notifier handoff
Chat Notifier to Chat Platform API

trust_boundaries.name: Internet to Event Receiver public endpoint
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between the external CI platform on the internet and the Deploy Notifier's public HTTPS Event Receiver endpoint.

trust_boundaries.name: Notifier to chat platform API boundary
trust_boundaries.description: Boundary between the Deploy Notifier components and the chat platform reached via its API.

questions.question: Will the Event Receiver be configured to verify CI platform signatures on deployment event deliveries, and if so which mechanism will be used?
questions.rationale: The documentation states that the CI platform supports signing webhook deliveries but that the receiver currently accepts any well-formed delivery without checking a signature (evd-003). Whether signature verification will be enabled affects the authentication status of the CI-to-Receiver data flow and the trust placed in incoming events.

questions.question: Are there any network-level controls (such as IP allowlists, VPN, or private ingress) or additional authentication mechanisms restricting access to the Event Receiver's public HTTPS endpoint beyond basic HTTPS?
questions.rationale: The Event Receiver is described as a public HTTPS endpoint that accepts and processes any well-formed JSON delivery without verifying a signature (evd-002, evd-003). Knowing whether other controls restrict who can reach this endpoint changes the effective exposure and threat model at this trust boundary.

questions.question: How are calls from the Chat Notifier to the chat platform API authenticated and encrypted, and is the chat platform an internally operated service or an external SaaS provider?
questions.rationale: The documentation notes that the Chat Notifier posts deployment events to an internal chat channel over the chat platform's API (evd-002) but does not specify whether HTTPS/TLS is used, what authentication mechanism protects the API, or whether the chat platform is internal or third-party. These details affect the trust boundary definition and the protection of deployment event data in transit and at the chat platform.
